cards.text: The prophet Ezekiel says the word of the LORD came to him in the eleventh year, on the first day of the third month. God tells him to speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his multitude, and the message opens with a question: "Who can be compared to your greatness?" Friend, in the junk drawer the nicest thing anybody ever said to me was "What is THIS?"

cards.question: God tells Pharaoh to look at a nation pictured as a cedar in Lebanon. Which nation is it?

cards.text: And WHAT a cedar: beautiful branches shading the forest, its top way up among the clouds. Friend, this tree doesn't have a top. It has a weather forecast.

cards.question: A tree that grows up into the clouds needs a LOT to drink. What does God say made this cedar grow so tall?

cards.text: With all that water, it towers higher than all the trees of the field, and its boughs grow long. This is the guy who gets sent to the back row of EVERY group photo.
And everybody wants a spot. All the birds of the air nest in its branches, and all the beasts of the field give birth beneath its boughs.

cards.question: All the great nations lived in the cedar's ___.
The cedars in the garden of God could rival this great cedar.

cards.text: This cedar is the envy of all the trees of Eden, in the garden of God. Every one of them is looking at it like the coworker who just got the corner office.

cards.question: God says the great cedar made itself beautiful.

cards.text: After all that praise for the great cedar, the word "Therefore" shows up. You know when a performance review is ALL compliments and you can FEEL the "however" coming?

cards.question: After all that praise, what does God hold against the great cedar?

answers.text: It grew proud of its height
It drank up all the water

cards.text: So God delivers it into the hand of the ruler of the nations, to deal with it according to its wickedness. Then God says, "I have banished it."
Foreigners, the most ruthless of the nations, cut it down and leave it, with its branches fallen on the mountains and in every valley. TIMBERRR.

cards.question: After the great cedar is cut down, all the peoples of the earth stay in its shade.
The birds of the air used to nest in the great cedar's branches. Where do they nest now that it's down?
God says the great cedar was cut down so other trees could grow even taller.

cards.text: On the day it's brought down to Sheol, God causes mourning. He holds back its rivers, and its abundant waters are restrained.
God makes Lebanon mourn for it, and all the trees of the field faint because of it.

cards.question: God made the nations ___ at the sound of the cedar's downfall.
Down in the earth below, all the trees of Eden are consoled. They went down to Sheol with the great cedar too. Who were they to the cedar?

cards.text: Then God turns back to Pharaoh with a question a lot like the one He opened with: "Who then is like you in glory and greatness among the trees of Eden?"

cards.question: God tells Pharaoh that he will be brought down to the depths of the earth too, to lie with those slain by the sword.

cards.text: Then God spells it out: "This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord GOD." So who compares with Pharaoh's greatness? A giant tree lying in pieces, and friend, that's not a compliment. That's a WARNING.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "What is THIS?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The question's setup, 'A tree that grows up into the clouds needs a LOT to drink,' points straight to water and rules out the soil and sun answers before the baker reasons anything out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'branches' is too close to the right answer 'shade.' Card 3 says the cedar's branches 'shaded the forest,' and card 6 has the birds living in its branches, so a baker could argue the nations lived in its branches.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: No card tells the second half of Ezekiel 31:14, that the trees 'have all been consigned to death, to the depths of the earth, among the mortals who descend to the Pit.' That half explains the move down to Sheol on the next card, and without it Sheol appears with no setup.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The card is a bare paraphrase of 31:15 with no trace of Papa Dorin's voice. With card 9, it makes two flat story cards in a row at the cedar's fall into Sheol.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card is a bare paraphrase of 31:15 (Lebanon mourns, the trees faint) with no trace of Papa Dorin's voice. It comes right after card 8, which is also flat.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: the quote, 'So who compares with Pharaoh's greatness?', 'A giant tree lying in pieces, and friend, that's not a compliment.', and 'That's a WARNING.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Calling the message a 'WARNING' adds a meaning the text doesn't give. Ezekiel 31:18 states what will happen: 'You also will be brought down to the depths of the earth.' A warning suggests Pharaoh could still avoid it, and the text leaves that open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
